description: The paired machine screens of the quality remediation (RF-50), read by scripts/quality_screen.py. A screen names its population; a rule is added here, with the date it was recorded, before any take it will judge is generated.

clone.description: Voice Clone through saved voices, the path both apps use: each reference is a human clip of a pinned, licensed corpus (config/audio-qc-corpora.json), enrolled with its corpus transcript, then asked for scripts of the committed CC0 pool in its own language and one in another language.

reference-preparation-v2.question: Does preparing a clone reference with the audio file reader and one converter call (QWENVOICE_REFERENCE_PREPARATION=single-call), in place of the asset reader's own decode and resampling, harm clones?
reference-preparation-v2.arms: A: the build's default path. B: the same build with the key set. Seed set 1, each arm in its own data directory, generated after this rule was recorded.
reference-preparation-v2.requires: Two B arms on the same seeds are identical on every take (compare --expect identical); arm A is not, which is the defect.
reference-preparation-v2.margins: About 1.4 times the widest bound the noise floor reached (0.035 similarity, 0.027 error rate, 25 ms, 3 failures). At 192 takes the screen separates a gross regression from no change and nothing finer: a change that passes is shown not to be grossly worse, not shown to be better.
reference-preparation-v2.decision: ADOPT when B is reproducible and no guard's interval reaches past its margin on the harmful side. REJECT when a guard's whole interval lies past its margin, or B loses more takes than allowed. Otherwise INCONCLUSIVE, and the default stays.

result.bReproducible: 190 of 190 takes identical; the default path twice (a1, a3) agreed on 167 of 191
result.note: Takes from references already at 24 kHz are identical in both arms (64 of 64). Trailing silence rose by 22 ms on average, the one guard whose interval excludes zero; its harmful end is 0.2 ms inside the margin.

encoder-rotary-split-half.question: Does encoding a clone reference with the split-half rotary convention the tokenizer's weights were trained for (QWENVOICE_ENCODER_ROTARY=split-half, A-02), in place of the adjacent-pair convention the port has always applied, harm transcript-backed clones?
encoder-rotary-split-half.arms: A: the build at the commit that adds the key, default convention. B: the same build with the key set. Seed set 1 of the clone screen, each arm in its own data directory, generated after this rule was recorded.
encoder-rotary-split-half.requires: The default arm A reproduces arm c1 (the default at a715b2ae) on every take, so adding the key changed nothing by default. Two B arms on the same seeds are identical on every take. scripts/encoder_golden_codes.py run with the key passes --expect reference, so the key reaches the encoder. The clone screen's noise floor (compare-a1-vs-s2.json, passed with --floor) sits inside 0.71 of each margin.
encoder-rotary-split-half.expected: No detectable change: the review's pre-screen in the Python port found +0.004 speaker similarity (interval -0.003 to +0.011) and an identical word error rate on 96 English pairs. The change is for parity with the reference encoder, so later comparisons start from the same codes.
encoder-rotary-split-half.decision: ADOPT when every requirement holds and no guard's interval reaches past its margin on the harmful side: the default then becomes split-half and the package's speaker-feature version gains an encoder version (G-03), so every transcript-backed prompt rebuilds once. REJECT when a guard's whole interval lies past its margin, or B loses more takes than allowed. Otherwise INCONCLUSIVE, and the default stays.

result.requirements: All held: ra reproduced c1 (a715b2ae) on 190 of 190 takes; rb1 and rb2 were identical on 190 of 190; the golden-codes pin passed --expect reference with the key (98.8% of codes, 99.6% of the first codebook) and --expect adjacent without it; the floor sat inside 0.71 of every margin.
result.grossFailuresOfB: Two French takes from English references entirely wrong (error rate 1.0), one German take of 0.32 s for a full sentence that passed Fast QC, and the two refused or incomplete takes both arms share in kind.
result.toolChange: Before the verdict, the screen tool was fixed (89d06485) to count a take too short for the speaker model as a gross failure instead of stopping; that made arm B's count stricter, not looser.
result.note: The error-rate interval excludes zero and reaches 0.001 past its margin; the noise floor's own error-rate shift was +0.012 (interval +0.0002 to +0.027), so the screen cannot tell this from seed noise at 0.04. The direction points at harm, chiefly in cross-language clones. The default stays the adjacent-pair convention; A-02 is not adopted.

reference-padding-none.question: Does encoding a clone reference as it is (QWENVOICE_REFERENCE_PADDING=none), as upstream Qwen3-TTS does, in place of appending half a second of zeros before the codec encodes it (A-12, Vocello's own step), harm transcript-backed clones?
reference-padding-none.arms: A: the build at the commit that adds the key, default padding. B: the same build with the key set. Seed set 1 of the clone screen, each arm in its own data directory, generated after this rule was recorded.
reference-padding-none.requires: The default arm A reproduces arm ra (the default at e8a25662) on every take, so adding the key changed nothing by default. Two B arms on the same seeds are identical on every take. The clone screen's noise floor (compare-a1-vs-s2.json, passed with --floor) sits inside 0.71 of each margin. B differs from A on its takes; arms that should differ and do not are INERT, never ADOPT.
reference-padding-none.expected: Unknown. The padding was added so a clone would not inherit a truncated final phoneme from the reference; that was never measured. Without it, the reference codes end where the clip ends, as upstream's do.
reference-padding-none.decision: ADOPT when every requirement holds and no guard's interval reaches past its margin on the harmful side: the default then encodes the reference unpadded and codecEncodeConditioningVersion is raised, so every transcript-backed prompt rebuilds once. REJECT when a guard's whole interval lies past its margin, or B loses more takes than allowed. Otherwise INCONCLUSIVE, and the default stays.

result.aReproducesDefault: pa is identical to ra (the default at e8a25662) on every take
result.bReproducible: pb1 and pb2 identical on every take
result.note: Not worse beyond any margin. The similarity and error-rate moves are the size of the screen's own noise floor (a1 against s2: similarity -0.015, error rate +0.012), so neither is evidence of a change; the shorter trailing silence lies mostly outside the floor's interval. B's two extra gross failures are English references asked for French (error rates 0.78 and 1.0); the third is a German voice that also failed under the rotary screen. Adopted: the reference is encoded as upstream encodes it, and codecEncodeConditioningVersion moves to icl-ref-unpadded-v3, so every transcript-backed prompt rebuilds once.

clone-decoder-history-primed.question: Does decoding a streamed transcript-backed clone with the reference's history (QWENVOICE_CLONE_DECODER_HISTORY=primed: the reference codes are decoded first and their samples discarded, as the quality-first path and upstream's ICL decode do) in place of a cold decoder harm clone takes (A-04, A-26)?
clone-decoder-history-primed.arms: A: the build at the commit that adds the key, default (a cold decoder). B: the same build with the key set. Seed set 1 of the clone screen, each arm in its own data directory, generated after this rule was recorded.
clone-decoder-history-primed.requires: The default arm A reproduces arm wa (the default at 1651e871) on every take, so adding the key changed nothing by default. Two B arms on the same seeds are identical on every take. Every paired take has the same length in A and B (requiresSameDuration): priming acts in the decoder only, so the talker's codes cannot move. The clone screen's noise floor (compare-a1-vs-s2.json, passed with --floor) sits inside 0.71 of each margin; because A and B decode the same codes, their paired differences carry no sampling noise and that floor is a conservative bound. B differs from A on its takes; arms that should differ and do not are INERT, never ADOPT.
clone-decoder-history-primed.expected: Unknown. A cold decoder acts most on a take's first frames; the upstream report of audible harm (QwenLM issue 219) was withdrawn by its author. Priming costs decoding the reference once per take before the first audio; it is reported, not judged.
clone-decoder-history-primed.decision: ADOPT when every requirement holds and no guard's interval reaches past its margin on the harmful side: streamed transcript-backed clones then prime by default, and with the decoder window adopted they prime from only the frames the window reaches (A-26). REJECT when a guard's whole interval lies past its margin, or B loses more takes than allowed. Otherwise INCONCLUSIVE, and the default stays.

result.aReproducesDefault: ha is identical to wa on every take
result.bReproducible: hb1 and hb2 identical on every take
open: 51 paired takes changed length, so the change reached the talker
result.note: The one open requirement is a proxy that does not hold for clones: the talker's own code count is identical on all 191 paired takes (engine rows, qwen_generated_code_count), and the 51 takes that changed length are exactly those whose clone onset trim (clone_leading_silence_trimmed_frames) changed, because priming changes the decoder's first frames, which the onset gate reads. Every guard is well inside its margin, and speaker similarity rose by +0.060, about twelve times the noise floor's mean shift. By the letter of the rule the default stays; clone-decoder-history-primed-confirm decides it on fresh seeds with the talker's code count as the requirement.

clone-decoder-history-primed-confirm.question: Confirmation on fresh seeds: does decoding a streamed transcript-backed clone with the reference's history (QWENVOICE_CLONE_DECODER_HISTORY=primed) in place of a cold decoder harm clone takes (A-04, A-26)?
clone-decoder-history-primed-confirm.arms: A: the build at dcfa4de6, default. B: the same build with the key set. Seed set 2 of the clone screen (run clone-seeds2, whose seeds no arm of this build has used), each arm in its own data directory, generated after this rule was recorded.
clone-decoder-history-primed-confirm.requires: The same build's default reproduced wa on every take of seed set 1 (ha), and two B arms of this build were identical there (hb1, hb2). Every paired take keeps the talker's code count (requiresSameCodeCount, from the engine rows): priming acts in the decoder only, and a take's length is not the test, because a clone's onset trim reads the decoder's first frames. The clone screen's noise floor (compare-a1-vs-s2.json, passed with --floor) sits inside 0.71 of each margin. Edit rates are read bounded at 1 per script unit (the screen tool since 2026-11-11). B differs from A on its takes; arms that should differ and do not are INERT, never ADOPT.
clone-decoder-history-primed-confirm.expected: Seed set 1 moved speaker similarity +0.060 (+0.052 to +0.068) with every guard inside its margin; this run checks it was not those seeds.
clone-decoder-history-primed-confirm.decision: ADOPT when every requirement holds and no guard's interval reaches past its margin on the harmful side: streamed transcript-backed clones then prime by default. REJECT when a guard's whole interval lies past its margin, or B loses more takes than allowed. Otherwise INCONCLUSIVE, and the default stays.

result.commit: dcfa4de6 (executable 08527b4a12474d11, the build of ha and hb1)
result.note: Replicates seed set 1 (+0.060): priming a streamed clone's decoder with the reference raises speaker similarity by about 0.056, more than ten times the screen's noise floor shift, with the error rate unchanged and the talker untouched. Adopted: streamed transcript-backed clones prime by default.

code-predictor-8bit.question: Does the Swift engine repeat the review's pre-screen (an 8-bit code predictor under the 4-bit talker: speaker similarity +0.010, interval +0.002 to +0.019, 48 pairs) on the clone screen's six languages (QWENVOICE_CODE_PREDICTOR_BITS=8: the code predictor from the installed 8-bit sibling), and does it harm anything (RF-55)?
code-predictor-8bit.arms: A: the build at the commit that records this rule, default (the 4-bit code predictor). B: the same build with the key set. Seed set 1 of the clone screen, each arm in its own data directory, generated after this rule was recorded.
code-predictor-8bit.requires: The default arm A reproduces arm hb1 on every take (the primed decoder, adopted at 1a308d7e, is the default since). Two B arms on the same seeds are identical on every take. The clone screen's noise floor (compare-a1-vs-s2.json, passed with --floor) sits inside 0.71 of each margin. B differs from A on its takes. The code predictor feeds the talker's next frame, so takes may change length and code count; neither is required equal.
code-predictor-8bit.expected: Speaker similarity a little higher, as in the pre-screen; nothing else moves beyond its margin. Measured before this rule, on the M6 with fixed seeds: the 8-bit code predictor makes a clone take about 20% slower where the GPU bounds a frame (real-time factor 0.303 to 0.363 long, 0.366 to 0.439 medium, two rounds each) and costs little where the host bounds it (efficiency cores: -1% to +6.5%), for 56 MB more weights.
code-predictor-8bit.decision: This rule changes no default: an 8-bit code predictor needs a new Speed artifact, which is the maintainer's decision. REPEATED when no guard reaches past its margin on the harmful side and B's speaker-similarity interval lies wholly above zero; NOT REPEATED when no guard harms but the interval includes zero; HARM when a guard's whole interval lies past its margin or B loses more takes than allowed. The tool's ADOPT reads as no harm; the similarity interval then decides REPEATED or NOT REPEATED.

noiseFloor.method: The 192 takes under seed set 1 and again under seed set 2, the same build and data. A change to conditioning moves every take's sampling as a new seed does, so this is what no change at all looks like.
noiseFloor.sameSeedsTwice: 159 of 191 takes identical; the 32 that differ belong to the 8 voices whose reference the asset reader resampled differently in the two runs. The scorers gave identical values on identical samples (32-take smoke).

clone-stereo.description: The clone screen's 48 references, each saved as a two-channel WAV before it is enrolled: the first, third and every odd reference of a language with the same signal on both channels (a mono recording saved as stereo, the common case), the others with the signal on the left and silence on the right. Sample values are copied, not recomputed. Corpus references are all mono, so a change to how two channels become one is invisible to the clone screen.

reference-mixdown-average.question: Does mixing a two-channel reference by the mean of its channels (preparation version 3, QWENVOICE_REFERENCE_PREPARATION=single-call-average), as upstream Qwen3-TTS and the Python port do, in place of the sum over the square root of two (version 2, the shipped default), harm clones?
reference-mixdown-average.arms: A: the build's default (version 2). B: the same build with the key set. Seed set 1, each arm in its own data directory, generated after this rule was recorded. A second A arm at seed set 2 measures this screen's own noise floor.
reference-mixdown-average.requires: Two B arms on the same seeds are identical on every take. This screen's noise floor (A at seed set 1 against A at seed set 2, passed to compare with --floor) has no guard bound wider than 0.71 of its margin; otherwise the verdict is INCONCLUSIVE whatever the comparison says.
reference-mixdown-average.margins: The clone screen's margins, which are about 1.4 times the widest bound of its noise floor; this screen has the same size and references. It separates a gross regression from no change and nothing finer.
reference-mixdown-average.expected: On duplicate references B's prepared audio equals the mono source, and A's is 3 dB hotter and clipped wherever the source peaked above -3 dBFS. On left-only references B's is 3 dB quieter than A's. The strata are reported, not decided on.
reference-mixdown-average.decision: ADOPT when B is reproducible, the floor condition holds and no guard's interval reaches past its margin on the harmful side. REJECT when a guard's whole interval lies past its margin, or B loses more takes than allowed. Otherwise INCONCLUSIVE, and the default stays.

noiseFloor.withinShare: every bound inside 0.71 of its margin

result.strata: Report-only. Duplicate references: similarity -0.004 (-0.026 to +0.017), gross failures 3 and 3. Left-only references: similarity +0.015 (-0.010 to +0.038), gross failures 2 and 1.
result.note: Not grossly worse anywhere, and not shown better: the 3 dB of headroom the average restores on duplicate references did not move any metric beyond the noise. It is adopted for parity with upstream and the Python port, and because it never clips a source that did not clip.

clone-long.description: The clone screen's 48 references, each asked for two long takes in its own language: four sentences of the committed CC0 pool joined into one script (about 15 to 20 seconds), generated as one take. The clone screen's takes average about 4 seconds, shorter than the speech tokenizer decoder's 72-frame attention window (5.76 s at 12.5 Hz), so a change that acts only late in a take is invisible to it. speakerSimilarityLate scores only the speaker windows that start at 6 s or later.

decoder-window-72.question: Does decoding with upstream's attention window (QWENVOICE_DECODER_WINDOW=on: every decoder layer attends over the current frame and the 71 before it, as Qwen3-TTS's tokenizer decoder does) in place of attention over the whole take harm long clone takes (RF-54, A-03)?
decoder-window-72.arms: A: the build at the commit that adds the key, default (attention over the whole take). B: the same build with the key set. Seed set 1 of this screen, each arm in its own data directory, generated after this rule was recorded. The floor: A under seed set 1 against A under seed set 2.
decoder-window-72.requires: The build's default reproduces, on every take, the clone screen's arm of the last adopted conditioning default (pb1, since reference-padding-none was adopted before this screen's first take), so adding the key changed nothing by default. Two B arms on the same seeds are identical on every take. Every paired take has the same length in A and B (requiresSameDuration): the window acts in the decoder only, so the talker's codes, and each take's length, cannot move, and a change of length means the change reached the talker. This screen's noise floor (passed with --floor) sits inside 0.71 of each margin; because A and B decode the same codes, their paired differences carry no sampling noise and the cross-seed floor is a conservative bound. B differs from A on its takes; arms that should differ and do not are INERT, never ADOPT.
decoder-window-72.expected: Unknown. Past 72 frames the shipped decoder attends to keys at distances its weights were never trained on; upstream's decoder never does. The first 72 frames of every take decode identically under both arms.
decoder-window-72.decision: ADOPT when every requirement holds and no guard's interval reaches past its margin on the harmful side: the default then decodes with the window, which changes every take longer than 5.76 s, and the decoder's cache is bounded to the window next, a change that keeps the output identical. REJECT when a guard's whole interval lies past its margin, or B loses more takes than allowed. Otherwise INCONCLUSIVE, and the default stays.

result.aReproducesDefault: wa (this build's default on the clone screen) is identical to pb1 on every take
result.bReproducible: lb1 and lb2 identical on every take
result.sameDuration: 96 of 96 paired takes: the talker's codes did not move
open: errorRateBetterFamily: the interval reaches past the margin of 0.04
the noise floor of trailingSilenceMS (34.0) exceeds 0.71 of its margin
result.note: Every move is small: speaker similarity +0.002 whole and -0.0015 late, the worst window -0.003, trailing silence -0.1 ms. The error-rate interval is one take: german-07's four-sentence German take is a gross failure in both arms (late speaker similarity 0.12 in both) and both recognizers ran away transcribing it (edit rates 1.0 and 6.3 in A, 32.6 and 2.6 in B); without it the difference is about zero. That an unbounded per-take edit rate can carry a mean is a defect of the screen's metric, fixed after this decision for later rules. The default stays without the window; a later screen on fresh seeds can decide it with the bounded metric and a decoder-only floor recorded first.

noiseFloor.method: Arm la (seed set 1) against arm ls (seed set 2), the same build and data.
noiseFloor.note: The trailing-silence bound (34 ms) exceeds 0.71 of a 40 ms margin, so at this size the screen cannot decide that guard for a change that moves sampling.

voiceBriefs: A calm man in his forties with a low, warm voice, speaking clearly at an unhurried pace.
A bright young woman with a clear, friendly voice and lively, natural intonation.
An older woman with a soft, slightly husky voice who reads in a gentle, measured way.

long-form.description: Long-form projects as the apps run them (--long-form always: planned into segments of up to about 900 characters, each a streaming take, joined): per stratum four scripts of twenty pool sentences drawn from both halves of the pool (about 70 to 100 seconds, two segments or more), each once under the default Expressive variation and once under Consistent, with the same script. Built-in Voice in English, French and Japanese, and Voice Design in English. Scored by both ASR families over the joined output, the spread of its speaker windows (no reference), the segments' end reasons (a segment that ran to the frame cap is a gross failure) and their Fast QC warnings.

long-form-full-text.question: Does full-text conditioning for long-form segments (QWENVOICE_FULL_TEXT_CONDITIONING=on: each segment's whole text laid over the prefix, the reference's non_streaming_mode=True, as single takes already do since RF-21) in place of trailing text harm long-form projects (D1)?
long-form-full-text.arms: A: the build at the commit that records this rule, default (segments keep trailing text). B: the same build with the key set. Seed set 1 of this screen, each arm in its own data directory, generated after this rule was recorded. The floor: A under seed set 1 against A under seed set 2.
long-form-full-text.requires: Two B arms on the same seeds are identical on every take. This screen's noise floor (passed with --floor) sits inside 0.71 of each margin. B differs from A on its takes; arms that should differ and do not are INERT, never ADOPT.
long-form-full-text.expected: Unknown. RF-20's content screen (2026-10-16) found no failure in either layout but its full-text arm was under its own minimum size, and it ran before the subtalker fix of 2026-10-19. Single takes adopted full text on 2026-10-20 (RF-21); segments kept trailing text.
long-form-full-text.decision: ADOPT when every requirement holds and no guard's interval reaches past its margin on the harmful side: long-form segments then take full-text conditioning, as single takes do. REJECT when a guard's whole interval lies past its margin, or B loses more projects than allowed. Otherwise INCONCLUSIVE, and segments keep trailing text.

open: speakerWindowSpread: the interval reaches past the margin of 0.05
the screen's own floor exceeds 0.71 of every margin
result.note: Full text leaned better (error rate lower, three fewer gross failures) but the screen cannot decide at this size; segments keep trailing text. Full text did not touch the long-form failures under Consistent or in Japanese, which are the larger defect and are screened next.

noiseFloor.method: Arm fa (seed set 1) against arm fs (seed set 2), the same build and data.
noiseFloor.note: Too wide to decide a margin of 0.04, 0.05 or 0.5 at this size: refusals leave only 18 paired projects. Under Consistent 18 of 32 projects are refused across both seed sets (Expressive 4 of 32), and Japanese 12 of 16 (segments of about 70 s with 2.2 to 2.9 s silent gaps and slow delivery).
